title: Cytoskeleton Fluorescence Staining of Eukaryotic Cells
author: Alfredo Leonardo Porfirio-Sousa
materials: Move cells onto a chamber culture slide (Lab-Tek™ II Chamber Slide - Thermo Fisher Scientific - 154461) according to how the cells are being grown, see below.

If cells are growing on agar plates, cut block where there is dense area of cells. Place upside down on chamber culture slide (Lab-Tek™ II Chamber Slide - Thermo Fisher Scientific - 154461 or Nest Scientific 2 well slide 230122). Add 500µl of liquid media (same media as agar is made) and allow to sit for 00:15:00 to Overnight under normal incubation conditions. Check on the inverted microscope to see if your cells have adhered.

If cells are growing in liquid media in a tissue culture flask, scrap cells with a cell scraper to dislodge cells from tissue culture flask. Move 1 mL to each chamber of the chamber culture slide (Lab-Tek™ II Chamber Slide - Thermo Fisher Scientific - 154461). Allow to sit for 00:15:00 to Overnight under normal incubation conditions. Check on the inverted microscope to see if your cells have adhered
Prepare all reagents as listed in the materials section. Prepare FRESH primary and secondary antibody dilutions before you proceed. The blocking buffer may be made in bulk beforehand.

steps.title: Prepare paraformaldehyde
steps.instruction: Ensure 8 % paraformaldehyde solution is at room temperature before use.

steps.title: Remove agar (if present)
steps.instruction: If cells were grown on agar, gently lift the agar block and remove all agar fragments from the chamber.

steps.title: Discard old medium
steps.instruction: Aspirate the existing liquid from the chamber VERY gently and discard it into a bleach solution.

steps.title: Add fresh growth medium
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of the original liquid media (or the same media used to make the agar) to the side of each chamber, allowing the liquid to flow down onto the glass surface while keeping the cells attached.

steps.title: Fix cells with paraformaldehyde
steps.instruction: Gently add 500 µL of 8 % paraformaldehyde (room temperature) to the side of each chamber, letting it flow down onto the glass; this dilutes the solution to a final concentration of 4 % paraformaldehyde.

steps.title: Incubate fixation
steps.instruction: Incubate the chambers at room temperature for 10 minutes (00:10:00).

steps.title: Remove fixative
steps.instruction: Gently aspirate the fixative with a 1 mL pipette and discard.

steps.title: PBS wash (first series)
steps.instruction: Rinse each chamber by adding 500 µL PBS to the side, allowing it to flow down onto the glass. Perform three washes, each lasting 3 minutes (00:03:00).

steps.title: Aspirate wash buffer
steps.instruction: Gently aspirate the PBS with a 1 mL pipette and discard.

steps.title: Permeabilize cells
steps.instruction: Aspirate any remaining liquid with a 1 mL pipette and discard. Then add 500 µL of 0.5 % Triton™ X‑100 to each chamber and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes (00:05:00).

steps.title: PBS wash (post‑permeabilization)
steps.instruction: Rinse each chamber by adding 500 µL PBS to the side, allowing flow down onto the glass. Perform three washes, each lasting 3 minutes (00:03:00).

steps.title: Block non‑specific binding
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Serum Blocking Buffer to each chamber and incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes (00:10:00). If Serum Blocking Buffer is unavailable, use 1 X BSA Blocking Buffer instead.

steps.title: Apply primary antibody / control
steps.instruction: For the test chamber, add 500 µL of anti‑α‑tubulin primary antibody (monoclonal mouse, clone B‑5‑1‑2) diluted 1:500. For the negative‑control chamber, add 500 µL PBS. Incubate both chambers at room temperature for 30 minutes (00:30:00), bringing the total volume to 1 mL.

steps.title: First ActinGreen stain
steps.instruction: Add 2 drops of ActinGreen 488 nm ReadyProbes Reagent (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog R37110) to each chamber and incubate at room temperature for 30 minutes (00:30:00).

steps.title: Aspirate primary stain
steps.instruction: Gently aspirate the liquid from each chamber with a 1 mL pipette and discard.

steps.title: PBS wash (post‑primary)
steps.instruction: Rinse each chamber by adding 500 µL PBS to the side, allowing flow down onto the glass. Perform four washes, each lasting 5 minutes (00:05:00). Aspirate all liquid after the final wash.

steps.title: Apply secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of secondary antibody (Goat anti‑Mouse IgG (H + L), Alexa 594) diluted 1:1000 to each chamber. Incubate at room temperature for 15 minutes (00:15:00) in the dark (cover with a box).

steps.title: Second ActinGreen stain
steps.instruction: Add 2 drops of ActinGreen 488 nm ReadyProbes Reagent (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog R37110) to each chamber and incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes (00:10:00) in the dark.

steps.title: NucBlue nuclear stain
steps.instruction: Add 2 drops of NucBlue ReadyProbes (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog R37605) to each chamber and continue incubating at room temperature for 10 minutes (00:10:00) in the dark.

steps.title: PBS wash (post‑secondary)
steps.instruction: Rinse each chamber by adding 500 µL PBS to the side, allowing flow down onto the glass. Perform three washes, each lasting 5 minutes (00:05:00). Aspirate all liquid after the final wash.

steps.title: Remove chamber sides
steps.instruction: Detach the chamber sides using the removal tool supplied with the Lab‑Tek™ II Chamber Slide kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog 154461).

steps.title: Mount with Fluoromount‑G
steps.instruction: Place ~100 µL of Fluoromount‑G (Thermo Fisher Scientific, catalog 00‑4958‑02) on the sample, then lay a clean 1.5H coverslip (22 × 22 mm) over one side of the chamber area, allowing it to settle gently to avoid bubbles. Incubate at room temperature for 15 minutes (00:15:00) in the dark.

steps.title: Seal coverslip
steps.instruction: Apply transparent nail lacquer around the edges of the coverslip. Let the lacquer dry for 15 minutes (00:15:00) at room temperature, keeping the slide in the dark.

steps.title: Image and store slides
steps.instruction: Visualize the slide on a fluorescence microscope using DAPI, GFP, and TexasRed filter cubes (or on a confocal microscope with 405 nm, 488 nm, and 532/561 nm lasers). Store slides horizontally at 4 °C in the dark.
